_meta.indication: STRIVERDI RESPIMAT is a long-acting beta2-agonist indicated for long-term, once-daily maintenance bronchodilator treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), including chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trials 1 and 2 — two replicate, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 48-week trials
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, 48-week trials
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 40 years or older with COPD, smoking history of at least 10 pack-years, and moderate to very severe pulmonary impairment (post-bronchodilator FEV1 less than 80% predicted [GOLD II–IV] and FEV1/FVC less than 70%)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from pre-treatment baseline in FEV1 AUC0-3 and trough (pre-dose) FEV1 (after 12 weeks in Trials 1 and 2)
pivotal_trials.n: 3104 patients total across all four 48-week trials (Trials 1 and 2, Trials 3 and 4); a combined N specific to Trials 1 and 2 is not separately stated in the cited line
pivotal_trials.result: STRIVERDI RESPIMAT 5 mcg showed significant improvement in FEV1 AUC0-3hr vs placebo at week 12: Trial 1 difference 0.16 L (95% CI 0.12, 0.21); Trial 2 difference 0.13 L (95% CI 0.09, 0.18). Trough FEV1 difference: Trial 1 0.08 L (95% CI 0.04, 0.13); Trial 2 0.03 L (95% CI -0.01, 0.08)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trials 3 and 4 — two replicate, placebo- and active- (formoterol 12 mcg twice-daily) controlled, parallel group, 48-week trials
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active- (formoterol 12 mcg twice-daily) controlled, parallel group, 48-week trials
pivotal_trials.population: Patients 40 years or older with COPD, smoking history of at least 10 pack-years, and moderate to very severe pulmonary impairment (post-bronchodilator FEV1 less than 80% predicted [GOLD II–IV] and FEV1/FVC less than 70%)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from pre-treatment baseline in FEV1 AUC0-3 and trough (pre-dose) FEV1 (after 24 weeks in Trials 3 and 4)
pivotal_trials.n: 3104 patients total across all four 48-week trials (Trials 1 and 2, Trials 3 and 4); a combined N specific to Trials 3 and 4 is not separately stated in the cited line
pivotal_trials.result: STRIVERDI RESPIMAT 5 mcg showed significant improvement in FEV1 AUC0-3hr vs placebo at week 12 (Table 2 reports week-12 differences for all four trials; the primary endpoint in Trials 3 and 4 was assessed after 24 weeks): Trial 3 difference 0.18 L (95% CI 0.14, 0.22); Trial 4 difference 0.15 L (95% CI 0.11, 0.18). Trough FEV1 difference at week 12: Trial 3 0.08 L (95% CI 0.04, 0.12); Trial 4 0.06 L (95% CI 0.02, 0.10)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >=2% and more than placebo) were nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infection, bronchitis, urinary tract infection, cough, dizziness, rash, diarrhea, back pain and arthralgia. For STRIVERDI 5 mcg (n=876) vs placebo (n=885): nasopharyngitis 99 (11.3%) vs 68 (7.7%), upper respiratory tract infection 72 (8.2%) vs 66 (7.5%), bronchitis 41 (4.7%) vs 32 (3.6%), urinary tract infection 22 (2.5%) vs 9 (1.0%)
target_moa: Olodaterol is a long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonist (LABA) that binds and activates beta2-adrenoceptors in the airways, stimulating intracellular adenylyl cyclase to increase cyclic AMP (cAMP), which induces bronchodilation by relaxing airway smooth muscle; it has 241-fold greater agonist activity at beta2- vs beta1-adrenoceptors

boxed_warning.content: Asthma-Related Death: Long-acting beta2-adrenergic agonists (LABA) increase the risk of asthma-related death. A placebo-controlled US study with another LABA (salmeterol) showed an increase in asthma-related deaths; this is considered a class effect. STRIVERDI RESPIMAT is not indicated for the treatment of asthma

rems.type: FDA determined a REMS is not necessary for Striverdi Respimat to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks

advisory_committee.vote: Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) held January 29, 2013 voted favorably on approvability (15 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain); also voted favorably on efficacy (15 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain) and safety (15 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain)

summary.text: Standard 505(b) NDA for olodaterol received May 14, 2012. The application was discussed at a PADAC meeting on January 29, 2013 that voted 15 to 1 favoring approval. A Complete Response was issued 3/14/13 solely due to GMP/manufacturing facility deficiencies; after the sponsor resolved manufacturing issues and resubmitted, the NDA was approved based on adequate clinical data demonstrating efficacy and LABA-class safety in COPD

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received May 14, 2012, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Striverdi Respimat (olodaterol) Inhalation Spray.
This application was also discussed a Pulmonary Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) meeting held on 1/29/13. The PADAC vote 15 to 1 favoring approval.

A Complete Response action was taken during the initial review cycle as manufacturing and testing facilities associated with the drug substance and drug product did not receive an acceptable GMP recommendation from the Office of Compliance, which precluded approval.
Boehringer-Ingelheim has resubmitted their NDA for olodaterol inhalation solution (Olo) following a Complete Response (CR) action taken on 3/14/13.

basis.text: Manufacturing and testing facilities associated with the drug substance and drug product did not receive an acceptable GMP recommendation from the Office of Compliance, which precluded approval

citations.quote: The CR action was taken as manufacturing and testing facilities associated with the drug substance and drug product did not receive an acceptable GMP recommendation from the Office of Compliance. This precluded approval in the initial review cycle, despite adequate clinical data to support the safety and efficacy of Olo for its proposed indication.
